Yavapai

Yavapai is a people-level reading route, not a substitute for distinct governments. The Yavapai-Apache Nation and Fort McDowell Yavapai Nation publish differently situated accounts of community life, displacement and collective action in Arizona.

02

A path for deeper reading

Read the sources [1] Yavapai-Apache Nation [2] yavapai-apache.org [3] yavapaiaz.gov

03

One Nation, two peoples

The Yavapai-Apache Nation identifies Yavapai and Apache as distinct peoples within its government and names five Verde Valley communities. These are not five separate governments or a census of every Yavapai community.

Read the sources [1] Yavapai-Apache Nation

04

Fort McDowell’s Orme Dam account

Fort McDowell’s history traces its community establishment to 1903. It describes residents organizing against the proposed Orme Dam and records a 1976 referendum before the 1981 cancellation announcement. This is the Nation’s account of a specific struggle, not a history of all Yavapai people.

Read the sources [4] Fort McDowell Yavapai Nation

05

Displacement and return in the Verde Valley

The Yavapai-Apache Nation describes the 1875 forced removal to San Carlos, dissolution of the earlier reservation and families’ eventual return. Its historical section places a 1909 trust acquisition within recovery from dispossession. Proposed exchanges elsewhere on the page do not establish present title or boundaries.

Read the sources [5] Yavapai-Apache Nation
